name: Birria Tacos Recipe
recipeIngredient: 4 pound boneless beef chuck (Or you can use beef shank or brisket - try with lamb shoulder. See Recipe Notes.)
16 corn tortillas (You can use flour tortillas.)
Fixings. Chopped red onion, sliced jalapeno or serrano, fresh chopped cilantro, chili flakes, fresh lime juice.

itemListElement.text: Heat a large pan to medium heat and add the dried peppers. Dry toast them in the hot pan 1-2 minutes per side, until the skins darken.
itemListElement.name: Dry Toast

itemListElement.text: Remove from heat and add the toasted peppers to a large bowl. Cover with hot water and steep 20 minutes, or until softened.
itemListElement.name: Soak

itemListElement.text: While the peppers are rehydrating, heat the olive oil in the same pan to medium heat.
itemListElement.name: Oil

itemListElement.text: Add the onion and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes to soften.
itemListElement.name: Onion and Tomatoes

itemListElement.text: Add the garlic and cook another 1 minute, stirring.
itemListElement.name: Garlic

itemListElement.text: Add the cooked onion, tomatoes and garlic to a food processor.
itemListElement.name: Food Processor

itemListElement.text: Remove the softened chilies and add to the food processor, but reserve the soaking liquid.
itemListElement.name: Softened Chilies

itemListElement.text: Add the seasonings to the food processor along with the vinegar and 1 cup beef stock. Process until smooth. It should be fairly thick, but you can thin if needed with the reserved soaking liquid. Strain if desired to remove any unprocessed bits of skin.
itemListElement.name: Process and Strain

itemListElement.text: Cut the beef into large chunks and add to a large bowl.
itemListElement.name: Cut Beef

itemListElement.text: Pour the birria sauce over them and rub it into the meat. Cover and marinate the meat in the refrigerator for 2 hours minimum. Overnight is better.
itemListElement.name: Marinate

itemListElement.text: Remove the beef from the marinade and sear in batches in your Dutch oven or large pot over medium-high heat with a tablespoon of oil, 2-3 minutes per side until browned. Don't discard the marinade.
itemListElement.name: Sear

itemListElement.text: Once all the beef is seared, add the reserved marinade, chopped roasted tomatoes and remaining 3 cups beef broth. Cover and cook at medium heat for 3 hours, or until the meat is fork tender and easy to shred. It should be fairly saucy.
itemListElement.name: Slow Cook

itemListElement.text: Shred the meat with forks to your preference. Reserve most of the birria sauce (consome).
itemListElement.name: Shred

itemListElement.text: Heat 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in a large pan or skillet. Dip the tortillas into the birria sauce (consome) to coat them evenly, then set them into the hot pan.
itemListElement.name: Dip Tortillas

itemListElement.text: Top with shredded birria meat. Fold the moistened shell over and fry 2-3 minutes until crisp, then flip over and fry the other side until crisp.
itemListElement.name: Top and Fry

itemListElement.text: Cool slightly and serve with your preferred toppings, with  reserved liquid consome from the pot as a side soup/broth.
itemListElement.name: Serve
